text:
Maya: Quick sync — need to lock perf work for next sprint. FinX (pilot customer) is pushing for ~80ms p95 + 2x throughput. We can’t hit both without tradeoffs. Decision needed: latency-first vs throughput-first?

Sam: Short take: latency-first via kernel+cache + quant looks highest impact for UX. effort = medium.

Jordan: Did a very rough RICE for two directions:
```
Option A (latency-first): kernel optimizations + KV prefix cache + 8-bit quant -> Reach p95 100–120ms 
R:8 I:7 C:5 E:5 -> (8*7)/(5+5)=5.6
Option B (throughput-first): auto-batching + sharded routing -> improve tokens/s overall
R:6 I:6 C:6 E:4 -> (6*6)/(6+4)=3.6
```
Numbers are approximate but show latency-first scores higher.

Liam: Note: Dedicated customers care a lot about cost/tokens; throughput wins there. Hosted customers and FinX care more about p95. Also infra risk: batching increases tail risk if misconfigured.

Eva: From CS: FinX will accept ~120ms p95 if we provide SLA language + clear rollback plan. They also want an estimate of cost delta.

Maya: Proposed scoped plan for next sprint:
- Phase 1 (priority): latency wins. Deliver kernel hotpath + KV prefix cache + opt-in 8-bit quant profile. Target p95 <= 120ms on canonical traces. Hosted only, feature-flagged route.
- Phase 2: if phase1 meets cost/quality gates, pursue batching/sharding for throughput.

Sam: Initial engineering estimate: 2 engineers x 3 weeks + 1 infra engineer for benchmarking & rollout infra. Effort still fuzzy for quant verification.

Jordan: Launch criteria (suggested):
- p95 <= 120ms on production-like traces (50k tokens sample)
- No quality regression on eval suite (100 seed prompts, automatic diff + human spotcheck)
- Token cost delta <= +10% (we can make up to +10% if UX gains justify it)
- Canary rollout with metrics alarms and automatic rollback if error rate or p95 regresses >10%

Sam: Implementation notes: add route-level trace hooks in Console, enable per-route caching TTL, add quantization verification job. Will push a draft design doc.

Maya: Negotiation: if we have to reduce scope to fit sprint, drop quantization from phase1 and keep it as opt-in experimental for a follow-up. That reduces risk and keeps timeline.

Liam: If quant is deferred, throughput path should be explicitly scheduled in the roadmap (phase2). Also add infra budget for burst capacity during canary.

Jordan: I'll add a quick checklist for quant eval: 
- Re-run evals on quantized model
- BLEU/ROUGE or embed-similarity threshold checks
- Latency + memory profiling
- Fallback plan to FP16 variant

Eva: I'll confirm FinX acceptance criteria for p95 and cost. Early signal: they said SLA + no more than 15% increase in monthly bill.

Maya: OK I'm going to convert this thread into a short PRD + RICE sheet. @Sam @Jordan please add engineering estimates and attach perf traces by EOD. If we can hit the estimates, we'll greenlight latency-first for the sprint. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Created issue INF-4023 for latency sprint planning — https://redwood.atlassian/INF-4023

Liam: One more: add post-deploy monitoring query to Console (p95, p99, tokens/s, token-cost) and hook alert to eng-oncall.

Jordan: Will add alerts and a canary dashboard.

Maya: Thanks all — final call in 11:00 sync.
